subject.title: Reject unpublished npm targets consistently in update dry-run

question: Should a confirmed public-npm HTTP 404 be a hard error for both update dry-run and apply, rather than a warning-only dry-run result followed by the package manager's normal apply failure?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible, but the PR deliberately changes an existing CLI compatibility boundary and repository policy requires maintainer intent for unconditional fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Accept strict 404 parity
options.body: Fail dry-run and apply before preview or service mutation when the actual public-npm install target is conclusively absent, while leaving transient errors non-blocking.

options.title: Warn during dry-run
options.body: Keep dry-run exit status compatible but emit an explicit unavailable-target warning, leaving apply to surface the package-manager failure.

recommendation.title: Accept strict 404 parity
recommendation.body: Fail dry-run and apply before preview or service mutation when the actual public-npm install target is conclusively absent, while leaving transient errors non-blocking.
